rows.label: Concept
rows.text: This chapter sets out the five types of essay - narrative, descriptive, expository, argumentative and persuasive - and the three-part structure common to all of them: an introduction with a hook and a thesis statement, body paragraphs built on a topic sentence with evidence and analysis, and a conclusion that restates the thesis and adds a final thought.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
An argumentative essay must be backed by evidence and logic; it is not mere personal opinion.
A descriptive essay should engage all five senses rather than only list facts.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Argumentative = personal opinion. ✅ Must be backed by evidence and logic.  ·  ❌ Descriptive = listing facts. ✅ Should engage all five senses.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Argumentative does NOT mean personal opinion - it must be backed by evidence and logic.  ·  Descriptive does NOT mean listing facts - it should engage all five senses.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Write an argumentative essay on 'Is technology beneficial or harmful?'  ·  Describe your favorite place using sensory details.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Check paragraph unity: every body paragraph must serve the thesis, so delete any paragraph that drifts from it.  ·  Before finishing a descriptive essay, confirm that all five senses appear.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Describe your favourite place using sensory details.  ·  Write an expository essay on 'The importance of education'.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Structure memory hook: 'Hook-Thesis, Topic-Evidence-Analysis, Restate-Summary-Final thought'.  ·  Word-count shortcut: 5-7 paragraphs of about 40-50 words each lands safely inside 250-300 words.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Write an argumentative essay on 'Is technology beneficial or harmful?' in 250-300 words.  ·  Write a narrative essay about an unforgettable event in your life.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The exam task is 5-7 paragraphs of 250-300 words on a common topic such as education, technology, environment, globalization, the role of youth, health, corruption or tourism in Nepal.  ·  Marks follow the structure, so never skip the introduction or the conclusion.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Five essay types: narrative, descriptive, expository, argumentative and persuasive  ·  Three-part structure: introduction, body paragraphs and conclusion  ·  Introduction: a hook plus a thesis statement  ·  Body paragraph formula: topic sentence + evidence + analysis

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Types: narrative tells a story with a sequence of events; descriptive paints a picture with words; expository explains objectively; argumentative presents a claim with evidence; persuasive convinces the reader.  ·  Introduction = hook + thesis statement.  ·  Body = topic sentence + evidence + analysis, with one main idea per paragraph.  ·  Conclusion = restate thesis + summary + final thought.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Write a persuasive essay on 'Why every student should read books'.  ·  Write an essay on 'Environmental protection is our duty' in 5-7 paragraphs.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: MCQ traps: 'an argumentative essay needs only personal opinion' and 'a descriptive essay is a list of facts' are both false.  ·  Keep one consistent register and check spelling and grammar; errors cost marks even when the content is correct.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Which part of an essay usually contains a hook and a thesis statement? → B  ·  What is the correct order of elements in a body paragraph? → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 1. Types of Essays  ·  - **Narrative**: Tells a story with a sequence of events  ·  - **Descriptive**: Paints a picture with words

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Conclusion: restate the thesis + summary + final thought  ·  Descriptive technique: sensory details of sight, sound, smell, touch and taste  ·  Descriptive technique: use sensory details and show rather than tell.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Argumentative technique: state a clear thesis, use credible evidence, address counterarguments and conclude forcefully.  ·  Underline the topic sentence of each paragraph when you finish; a missing one usually costs a mark.  ·  Every body paragraph needs a topic sentence that states the paragraph's main idea.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The introduction needs a hook to attract the reader and a clear thesis statement.  ·  The conclusion restates the thesis, summarizes the body and ends with a final thought.  ·  An expository essay explains or informs objectively.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Type test: does it tell a story (narrative), paint a picture (descriptive), explain (expository), argue with evidence (argumentative) or convince (persuasive)?  ·  To handle a counterargument, add one short paragraph that raises the opposite view and then answers it - this is what lifts an argumentative essay.  ·  Never introduce new information in the last sentence; conclude forcefully on the point already made.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: This chapter is about structure and technique; do not add grammar rules that are not in these notes.  ·  Write an essay of 250-300 words in 5-7 paragraphs on a prescribed topic.  ·  Write a persuasive essay that convinces the reader to accept a viewpoint.
